newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to decide securities tax changes by June - paper.
newsitem.headline: MOF to decide securities tax changes by June - paper.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) will likely reach a conclusion on how to revamp Japan's securities taxes by June, a senior ministry official was quoted by a Japanese newspaper as saying on Wednesday.

Atsushi Nagano, director-general of MOF's Securities Bureau, was quoted by the daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun as saying in an interview that MOF wants to submit bills needed for Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms to parliament in 1998.
Nagano also said MOF was not considering taking any steps to manipulate individual stocks, and that current stock movement deviated from the economic reality.

"Looking at production and jobs data, the economy at the moment remains firm. Corporate profits may slow, but are still expected to show double-digit growth, so that the market movement is deviating from the economic reality," Nagano was quoted as saying in the interview.
"We are not considering taking action to raise or lower individual stocks," he added.
Nagano said he was aware of market concerns about a possible delay in the government tackling economic reforms.

The MOF wants to submit bills needed for "Big Bang" financial deregulation during a regular parliamentary session starting in January 1998, he said. As for a possible revamp in Japan's securities taxes, the authorities have agreed to craft an outline by June, he added.
Nagano was quoted as saying that stock movements could affect Japan's economic fundamentals, so the ministry would continue to monitor the market with grave interest.

He also said he could not immediately tell whether a weak yen was good or bad for Japan stocks. "But I can imagine that some foreign investors may feel difficulties in investing in stocks before confirming the currency movements," he added.
